title: Review of Financial Assistance Provided to Low-Income Families Given Minimum Income Standard Report 2023
what_it_is: Review of Financial Assistance Provided to Low-Income Families Given Minimum Income Standard Report 2023

sections.label: ComCare assistance and minimum income
sections.summary: Asked whether MSF will adjust financial assistance to low-income families and study living wage levels; assistance quantum was last increased in August 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development in view of the findings in the Minimum Income Standard Report 2023, whether the Ministry will consider (i) adjusting the financial assistance rendered to low-income families and (ii) conducting its own study to determine the level of living wage required to support a basic standard of living using various Government data beyond what is publicly available.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We last increased the assistance quantum for the ComCare Short-to-Medium Term Assistance and Long-Term Assistance in August 2022.

sections.label: Minimum income standard and ComCare criteria
sections.summary: MIS 2023 set minimum income standard at $6,693 monthly for a household with two school-going children, about $1,600 per capita.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Minimum Income Standard Report 2023 (MIS) stated that the minimum income standard budget for a household with two school-going children is $6,693 per month or about $1,600 per capita.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Since MSF is giving ComCare assistance to the lowest 20th percentile of households, would MSF think that the $800 dollars per capita income, as a criterion to provide financial assistance, is too high or too low?

sections.label: Lower-income families financial help
sections.summary: Lower-income families qualify for and receive more financial help than median households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Lower-income families qualify for and receive more financial help than median households.

sections.label: ComCare basic package review
sections.summary: MSF assesses its basket of products and services for ComCare families from time to time, including mobile data plans for digital connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I also thank him for making me go through an exercise to jog my memory about what I said yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I remember saying in my reply to a Parliamentary Question (PQ) on ComCare that, actually, we assess our basket of products and services that are needed in a basic package for our ComCare families from time to time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: And we have included mobile data plans because they provide for digital connectivity which, in turn, provides for human connection, which is a basic need we assessed.

sections.label: Dignity of lower-income families
sections.summary: The speaker says not to underestimate lower-income families' agency, strength and dignity to break the cycle of poverty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Work hard for these things lor." So, my takeaway earlier from these two conversations is this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Let us not underestimate the agency, the strength and the dignity of our lower-income families and the ability to turn things around and to break the cycle of poverty – with them clearly in the loop, with them clearly holding on to the levers of their own lives.
